title: The Psychology of Learning Faster, Explained
desc: How do people really learn, and how can you learn almost anything faster and remember it for longer? A calm, sourced listen through the research: why rereading and highlighting barely work, the power of testing yourself, spacing, mixing topics, the trap of feeling sure, explaining to learn, deliberate practice and the ten thousand hour myth, mindsets, memory palaces, notes and reading, working memory, brain training, and sleep. Every claim comes from named studies, and the doubts are left in.
plan: b01: intro; study habits that barely work (Karpicke 2009, Dunlosky 2013)
b02: testing effect (Roediger & Karpicke 2006, Rowland 2014, Butler 2008)
b04: interleaving (Rohrer & Taylor 2007, Kornell & Bjork 2008, Rohrer 2015, Brunmair & Richter 2019)
b05: illusions of knowing (Rhodes & Castel 2008, Koriat & Bjork 2005, Kruger & Dunning 1999)
b06: explaining (Rozenblit & Keil 2002, Chi 1989/1994, Nestojko 2014, Fiorella & Mayer 2013)
b08: mindsets, productive failure (Mueller & Dweck 1998, Sisk 2018, Yeager 2019, Kapur 2014)
b10: notes, reading, learning styles (Mueller & Oppenheimer 2014, Urry 2021, Pashler 2008)
b11: working memory (Miller 1956, Cowan 2001, Chase & Simon 1973, Sweller)
b12: brain training (Owen 2010, Simons 2016, ACTIVE, Erickson 2011)
b13: sleep, habits, curiosity (Jenkins & Dallenbach 1924, Gollwitzer & Sheeran 2006, Gruber 2014)
